metadata.repo_type_justification: pricing.cpp contains a deployable entry point (int main(void)) and the repo ships a Dockerfile plus k8s/ deployment manifests for a single service.
metadata.archetype_justification: No database driver, no writes, no message consumers. The single CGI entry point reads a static pipe-delimited file (/etc/pricing/rules.dat) and returns a computed price synchronously.
metadata.surface_flags_rationale: No DB resource or driver anywhere (pricing.cpp uses fopen on a baked-in flat file); no S3/EBS/EFS or AWS storage resource; Dockerfile plus k8s/deployment.yaml constitute a deployed workload; the CGI binary is served over HTTP:8080 via Apache; replicas: 2; no Terraform/CDK/CloudFormation present (only Kubernetes manifests).

classification.rationale: This repo has 3 High, 21 Medium, 1 Low findings. MOD classification is deliberately softer than ARA on '1 High': in ARA a single High is an agent-deployment gate, whereas in MOD a single High is typically one modernization gap and maps to Pilot-Ready. Here three High findings (INF-Q11, DATA-Q1, OPS-Q6) place the repo in Remediation Required. The score-based band (1.76 → Needs Work) agrees with the count-based tier.

top_gaps.title: CI/CD Automation
top_gaps.gap: No pipeline of any kind; Makefile's install target scp's the binary to deploy@pricing01.
top_gaps.impact: Every release is a manual, unauditable copy; no quality or security gate can be added until a pipeline exists.

top_gaps.title: Unstructured Data Storage
top_gaps.gap: Pricing rules live in a local flat file (/etc/pricing/rules.dat) baked into the image.
top_gaps.impact: Production pricing data has no source of truth, no versioning, and is lost on pod replacement.

top_gaps.title: Integration Testing
top_gaps.gap: No test files, no test target in the Makefile, no CI.
top_gaps.impact: Memory-unsafe C++ cannot be refactored or recompiled safely without regression coverage.

top_gaps.title: Observability (OPS-Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4/Q7/Q8)
top_gaps.gap: No tracing, metrics, SLOs, alarms, runbooks, or ownership artifacts anywhere in the repo.
top_gaps.impact: The service is operationally blind; incidents are detected by customers.

top_gaps.title: API Authentication / Security Pipeline (SEC-Q3, SEC-Q7)
top_gaps.gap: CGI endpoint is unauthenticated; no SAST, dependency, or container scanning despite a known strcpy overflow.
top_gaps.impact: Reflected unescaped output plus unbounded strcpy is remotely exploitable with no detection.

pathways.not_triggered_reason: No AI/agent intent evidenced in the repository (no AI-related signal terms in dependencies, source, configuration, IaC, or documentation). Contextual guard blocks evaluation of the primary trigger.

findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: Workload is containerized and targets managed orchestration: Dockerfile is a multi-stage build (gcc:12 -> httpd:2.4-alpine) and k8s/deployment.yaml runs it as a Deployment with 2 replicas; CONTAINERIZE.md documents ECR push and kubectl apply to EKS. No aws_instance or EC2 user-data exists. However no IaC provisions the cluster, and the image reference is still the placeholder legacy-pricing-cgi:latest. The managed-compute target is declared but not provisioned or pinned.
findings.gap: No cluster/node/Fargate-profile definition in IaC, and an unresolved image tag means the manifests cannot deploy as committed.
findings.recommendation: Add IaC for the EKS cluster (or an ECS/Fargate task definition) and the ECR repository, then replace legacy-pricing-cgi:latest with the immutable ECR image digest in k8s/deployment.yaml.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: The repo owns a Kubernetes network surface only. k8s/service.yaml is correctly type: ClusterIP and k8s/namespace.yaml gives the workload a dedicated namespace, but no NetworkPolicy exists so all in-cluster pods can reach port 8080. The commented-out Ingress example specifies scheme: internet-facing with no WAF or auth annotation.
findings.gap: No default-deny NetworkPolicy and no segmentation; the documented ingress path would expose an unauthenticated, memory-unsafe CGI binary directly to the internet.
findings.recommendation: Add a default-deny ingress NetworkPolicy in the legacy-pricing-cgi namespace allowing only the ingress controller on 8080. If the ALB Ingress is adopted, attach AWS WAF and prefer scheme: internal until the strcpy overflow in parse_query is fixed.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: The only committed entry point is a ClusterIP Service on port 8080 fronting Apache mod_cgi. An ALB Ingress exists solely as commented-out YAML, and no API Gateway, AppSync, CloudFront, or aws_lb_* resource exists in the repo. No managed entry point is actually configured, so there is no throttling, request validation, authentication, or WAF.
findings.gap: No throttling, no request validation, no auth, and no WAF in front of a CGI parser with no bounds checking.
findings.recommendation: Create the ALB Ingress (or front the service with API Gateway) and configure request size limits, rate limiting, and an authorizer. Edge request validation is the fastest mitigation for the unbounded query-string parsing in parse_query.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: k8s/deployment.yaml pins replicas: 2 statically. No HorizontalPodAutoscaler, VerticalPodAutoscaler, Karpenter/Cluster Autoscaler config, or aws_appautoscaling_* resource exists (searched k8s/ and repo root for *.tf). CPU/memory requests and limits are set (100m/64Mi -> 500m/128Mi), which would give an HPA its signal but is not itself scaling.
findings.gap: Capacity is entirely static; a traffic spike on a per-request fork/exec CGI model cannot be absorbed.
findings.recommendation: Add an HPA on CPU and request rate with min 2 / max N replicas. Because CGI forks a process per request, load-test to set limits.cpu appropriately before enabling scaling.

findings.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
findings.description: Two replicas with readiness and liveness probes make a single pod failure survivable, but there is no topologySpreadConstraints, no pod anti-affinity, and no PodDisruptionBudget, so both replicas may land on one node in one AZ. No AZ/subnet configuration exists (no IaC). README.md describes the current production state as a single Solaris/EC2 host.
findings.gap: Multi-AZ fault isolation is not explicit - replica placement is unconstrained and voluntary disruptions are unguarded.
findings.recommendation: Add topologySpreadConstraints across topology.kubernetes.io/zone with maxSkew: 1, plus a PodDisruptionBudget of minAvailable: 1.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: Kubernetes manifests cover the workload surface (namespace, configmap, deployment, service), but has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources is false - no .tf, CDK, CloudFormation, SAM, or Helm chart exists. The ALB Ingress the repo depends on is only a comment in k8s/service.yaml, and the ECR repository, cluster, and all operational/DR resources have no IaC. CONTAINERIZE.md directs the operator to run docker build/push and kubectl apply by hand and to hand-edit the image URI.
findings.gap: Registry, cluster, ingress, and monitoring resources are created out-of-band, so the deployment is not reproducible from the repo.
findings.recommendation: Add Terraform or CDK covering ECR, the ingress/ALB, and CloudWatch alarms; package the k8s manifests as a Helm chart or Kustomize overlay so the image tag and namespace are parameterized rather than hand-edited.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No pipeline definitions exist - searched for .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml, appspec.yml; none present. The sole committed deployment mechanism is Makefile's install target: scp $(TARGET) deploy@pricing01:/var/www/cgi-bin/pricing.cgi. README.md confirms deployment is scp the binary and restart Apache; CONTAINERIZE.md documents the container path as manual operator commands.
findings.gap: Both application and infrastructure deployments are fully manual with no build, test, or deploy automation and no rollback path.
findings.recommendation: Create a pipeline: compile (make all) -> automated tests -> container build -> ECR push with scan-on-push -> deploy to EKS -> automated rollback on failed probes. Remove the scp-based install target so manual host copies are no longer possible.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: Compound legacy signals on all three axes. Language: C++ pre-C++11 (cstdio/cstring, strcpy, strtok, sscanf; header records 2004, last build 2016 with GCC 3.4). Framework: Apache CGI (mod_cgi enabled in Dockerfile), a pre-modern execution model with no web framework. SDK: no AWS SDK dependency at all; build is a hand-written Makefile with no dependency manager.
findings.gap: C++ here has no AWS SDK integration and limited cloud-native tooling depth; the CGI model plus the GCC 3.4 toolchain assumption requires a language-standard upgrade, a framework replacement, and SDK introduction.
findings.recommendation: Compile to C++17 or later with -fstack-protector-strong -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 -Wall -Wextra and replace raw char buffers with std::string/std::string_view. Then evaluate replacing the CGI transport with a long-lived HTTP service rather than forking a process per request.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: A single deployable unit: one Dockerfile, one Deployment, one compiled artifact. Within pricing.cpp three concerns are identifiable (parse_query, lookup_price, main/rendering) but are not separated behind interfaces: parse_query writes into caller-owned fixed char buffers, lookup_price hardcodes its own data source path, and main renders HTML inline with printf. No shared database and no cross-module data coupling.
findings.gap: Identifiable concerns with no module boundaries or interfaces - data source, parsing contract, and presentation format are hardwired into one translation unit, so none can change independently.
findings.recommendation: Apply Hexagonal Architecture within the single unit: a PriceRepository interface (file today, S3/DynamoDB later), a parsing type returning a validated value object instead of filling raw buffers, and a renderer separated from the calculation. Strengthening as a modular monolith is the recommended path, not microservice extraction.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: The single endpoint is /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi?sku=...&qty=... There is no /v1/ path segment, no version header handling in pricing.cpp, no OpenAPI/Swagger spec, and no CHANGELOG. The response is unstructured HTML emitted by printf, so even the response shape is an implicit contract.
findings.gap: No versioning at all - any change to query parameters or the HTML response breaks every consumer simultaneously, and consumers must scrape HTML to obtain the price.
findings.recommendation: Expose /v1/price returning JSON, publish an OpenAPI spec in the repo, and keep the existing CGI path as a deprecated v0 alias behind an Anti-corruption Layer until consumers migrate.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: k8s/configmap.yaml externalizes PRICING_RULES_PATH and SERVER_NAME via envFrom, and the Service name provides Kubernetes DNS for inbound callers. But pricing.cpp ignores the ConfigMap: lookup_price hardcodes fopen("/etc/pricing/rules.dat"), and Makefile hardcodes the host deploy@pricing01. No Cloud Map, Consul, or service mesh is configured.
findings.gap: Configuration is env-var-based with no dynamic discovery, and the externalized variable is not actually consumed - the data-source path is hardcoded in the binary, so the ConfigMap is inert.
findings.recommendation: Make lookup_price read PRICING_RULES_PATH from the environment with the current literal as a fallback so the ConfigMap becomes effective. Remove the hardcoded pricing01 host from Makefile. Use Kubernetes DNS or AWS Cloud Map for any future outbound dependency.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: The pricing rule set - the service's entire business data - is a pipe-delimited flat file on the container's local filesystem. pricing.cpp opens /etc/pricing/rules.dat directly and Dockerfile bakes a one-line placeholder into the image (SAMPLE-SKU|9.99). No aws_s3_bucket, no S3 SDK call, no PVC, and no parsing pipeline exist. README.md states rules are edited in-place on prod with no source of truth.
findings.gap: Business-critical data lives on local, ephemeral, unversioned storage with no source of truth, audit trail, or durability - and the shipped image contains sample data, so a deploy as-committed would serve sample prices.
findings.recommendation: Move the rule set to S3 (versioning + Object Lock) or DynamoDB as the source of truth, abstracted behind the PriceRepository interface from APP-Q2. In the interim mount it from a version-controlled ConfigMap and remove the sample row from the image.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: Data access is inline with no abstraction: lookup_price performs fopen/fgets/sscanf/fclose and parses the record format ("%[^|]|%lf") in the same function called from main. There is no repository, DAO, or adapter type, and the parse result is written into a fixed char file_sku[MAX_SKU] with an unbounded %[^|] conversion.
findings.gap: Storage mechanism, record format, and lookup logic are fused, which is what blocks the DATA-Q1 move to S3/DynamoDB. The unbounded sscanf conversion is also a latent overflow on any rules line with a long SKU field.
findings.recommendation: Extract a single PriceRepository abstraction with one implementation per backing store; add a field-width limit to the sscanf format (%63[^|]) as an immediate safety fix.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: The endpoint is fully open. Dockerfile configures the CGI directory with Require all granted and Options +ExecCGI and no authentication module; pricing.cpp reads only QUERY_STRING via getenv and performs no token, header, or credential check. No API Gateway authorizer, Cognito pool, or auth middleware exists in the repo.
findings.gap: Every request is unauthenticated and unattributable. Combined with the unbounded strcpy(buf, qs) in parse_query and unescaped reflection of sku into HTML, an anonymous caller reaches a memory-unsafe parser and an XSS sink.
findings.recommendation: Terminate authentication at the edge first - API Gateway with a JWT/Cognito authorizer or an ALB with OIDC - and keep the Service ClusterIP-only. Fix the buffer handling in parse_query in parallel; auth reduces exposure but does not remove the overflow.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: No identity provider integration of any kind. Searched pricing.cpp, k8s/, and Dockerfile for Cognito, OIDC, SAML, or federation configuration - none found. The application has no notion of a user or principal; it neither manages its own authentication nor federates to an external IdP.
findings.gap: There is no identity surface to attach to central access policy, so access cannot be governed, revoked, or audited per-consumer.
findings.recommendation: When SEC-Q3 authentication is introduced, implement it against the organization's central IdP (Cognito machine-to-machine pools, or Okta/Ping via OIDC) rather than service-local credentials.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: Meaningful hardening exists: Dockerfile creates and switches to a non-root appuser, and k8s/deployment.yaml sets runAsNonRoot, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, capabilities.drop: [ALL], and resource limits. But there is no patching automation and no vulnerability scanning: no Dependabot or Renovate config, no Inspector/Snyk, no ECR scan-on-push, no SSM Patch Manager, and base image tags are floating rather than digest-pinned.
findings.gap: Hardening is present but patching is entirely manual - nothing detects a CVE in httpd:2.4-alpine or rebuilds on publication. readOnlyRootFilesystem and seccompProfile are also unset.
findings.recommendation: Enable ECR scan-on-push, add Renovate/Dependabot for the Dockerfile base images, pin base images by digest, and add readOnlyRootFilesystem: true (with an emptyDir for Apache logs) and seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault to the pod security context.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: There is no pipeline at all and therefore no security validation step: no SAST (no SonarQube, Semgrep, CodeGuru, cppcheck, or clang-tidy config), no dependency scanning (no dependabot.yml, renovate.json, .snyk), and no container image scanning. Makefile compiles with -O2 -Wall only - no -Wextra, no sanitizers, no hardening flags.
findings.gap: A codebase with documented memory-safety defects (README.md lists unsafe strcpy/sprintf and no bounds checking on query-string parsing, both confirmed in parse_query) has zero automated detection.
findings.recommendation: Add a blocking C/C++ SAST gate (clang-tidy cert-*/bugprone-* or Semgrep C++ rules), ASan/UBSan builds in the test stage, ECR image scanning, and base-image dependency updates. Add -Wextra -Werror -fstack-protector-strong -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 to CXXFLAGS.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No tracing instrumentation. pricing.cpp has no OpenTelemetry or X-Ray SDK usage (only cstdio/cstdlib/cstring are included) and never reads traceparent or X-Amzn-Trace-Id from the CGI environment. No sidecar, ADOT collector, or trace exporter is configured in k8s/deployment.yaml.
findings.gap: No trace IDs are generated or propagated, so requests cannot be correlated across the ingress -> Apache -> CGI path or with upstream callers.
findings.recommendation: Read the inbound HTTP_TRACEPARENT/HTTP_X_AMZN_TRACE_ID CGI environment variables and emit them in structured log lines as a first step; pair with an ADOT collector once the service becomes a long-lived process.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No monitoring artifacts exist in the repo - no SLO definition files, no CloudWatch alarms (no IaC at all), no ServiceMonitor/PrometheusRule, no error-budget tracking. The only health signals are the readiness and liveness probes in k8s/deployment.yaml, which are liveness checks rather than latency or error-rate thresholds, so the Score-2 condition is not met.
findings.gap: There is no stated or measured definition of acceptable availability or latency for the pricing endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Define an availability and p99 latency SLO for GET /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi and express it as CloudWatch alarms (or PrometheusRule) committed alongside the new IaC, with error-budget tracking.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics are emitted. pricing.cpp writes only the HTML response via printf - no put_metric_data, no StatsD/Prometheus client, no /metrics endpoint. Business-relevant events are unrecorded; notably lookup_price returns 0.0 both when the rules file is unreadable and when the SKU is unknown, which is silently indistinguishable.
findings.gap: No business-outcome telemetry; the unknown-SKU and rules-file-unreadable failure modes are invisible and are served to callers as a $0.00 price.
findings.recommendation: Emit structured JSON log lines per request (sku, found/not-found, unit price, duration) and derive CloudWatch metric filters from them, including a dedicated alarm on the rules-file-unreadable path. Distinguish file-missing from SKU-not-found in lookup_price first.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting is configured. Searched k8s/ and the repo root for CloudWatch alarms, anomaly detectors, PrometheusRule/Alertmanager configuration, and PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration - none exist. Probe failures in k8s/deployment.yaml restart or de-register a pod but notify no one.
findings.gap: Failures are detected only by consumers; neither static thresholds nor anomaly detection exist on error rate or latency.
findings.recommendation: Start with static CloudWatch alarms on ingress 5xx rate and p99 latency routed to an on-call destination, then layer CloudWatch anomaly detection on request-rate and error-rate once a baseline exists.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy
findings.description: The repo owns deployment artifacts, so this is evaluated. k8s/deployment.yaml uses the implicit default RollingUpdate with working readiness and liveness probes on ?sku=HEALTH&qty=1 - rolling deployment with basic health checks. There is no traffic shifting: no canary, Argo Rollouts, CodeDeploy config, weighted target groups, or feature flags. CONTAINERIZE.md prescribes kubectl apply -f k8s/.
findings.gap: Health-check-gated rolling updates catch a crash-on-start but not a behavioral regression - with no tests, a bad pricing calculation would roll out to all traffic unnoticed. Rollback is manual.
findings.recommendation: Adopt progressive delivery (Argo Rollouts or ALB weighted target groups) with an automated analysis step comparing the canary's price output against the stable version for a fixed SKU set, and automatic rollback on divergence.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: There are no automated tests of any kind. The repo contains one source file and no test directory, test framework dependency, or test target - Makefile has only all, install, and clean. README.md states: No tests; correctness validated by spot-checking output. With no CI there is nothing to run tests in either.
findings.gap: No regression safety net for a memory-unsafe binary that cannot be rebuilt reproducibly. This blocks every other recommendation: C++ modernization, the repository abstraction, the S3 rule-store move, and progressive delivery all require tests to be safe.
findings.recommendation: Write characterization tests first: capture current output for a fixed matrix of sku/qty inputs (including missing params, unknown SKU, non-numeric qty, oversized query strings) into golden files, then add an integration test that runs the built container and asserts HTTP responses against them. Wire both into CI as a blocking gate.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation
findings.description: No runbooks or remediation automation exist. Documentation is README.md (architecture plus a Known Issues list) and CONTAINERIZE.md (build/deploy instructions); neither contains incident procedures, and there are no SSM Automation documents, Lambda remediations, or Step Functions workflows. README.md documents live hazards - in-place prod rule edits, per-request memory leaks, an unreproducible build - with no response procedure.
findings.gap: Incident response is entirely ad hoc for a service whose known failure modes are already enumerated but unaddressed.
findings.recommendation: Write versioned in-repo runbooks for the documented failure modes (rules file missing/corrupt, pod OOM from the per-request leak, rollback of a bad image), then automate the highest-frequency one as an SSM Automation document.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No ownership artifacts. There is no CODEOWNERS file, no dashboards or alarms to own, and no owner/team metadata on any resource - the manifests carry only app.kubernetes.io/name, component, and part-of labels. The sole human reference is the 2004 author comment in pricing.cpp and the README.md pointer to see ops.
findings.gap: No team is identifiably accountable for this service's monitoring, so gaps and alerts have no owner.
findings.recommendation: Add a CODEOWNERS file, add owner/team labels to the Kubernetes manifests (propagated as CloudWatch dimensions/tags), and name an owning team in README.md alongside the dashboards created for OPS-Q2.

evaluations.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - archetype-calibrated: synchronous request/response is the correct design for a stateless-utility. The CGI is invoked synchronously per HTTP request (k8s/service.yaml port 8080, mod_cgi in Dockerfile) and emits no outbound signals; no self-managed broker is present, which is the correct outcome for this archetype. Adopting async is explicitly not recommended.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - no stored procedures, triggers, or proprietary SQL. No .sql files and no CREATE PROCEDURE/TRIGGER/FUNCTION statements; all pricing logic (unit * qty) is in the application layer in pricing.cpp.

evaluations.title: Secrets Management
evaluations.reason: Score 4 - no credentials anywhere in the repo. k8s/configmap.yaml holds only non-secret config; pricing.cpp has no credential literals or connection strings; .gitignore excludes .env and .env.*; CONTAINERIZE.md records that no secrets are required and directs future credentials to Kubernetes Secrets.

evaluations.title: Workflow Orchestration
evaluations.reason: Archetype-N/A: stateless-utility has no multi-step workflows - main() performs a single parse -> lookup -> render sequence per CGI invocation. Recorded as Not Evaluated rather than a default Score 4 to avoid score inflation.

evaluations.title: Async vs Sync Communication
evaluations.reason: Archetype-N/A: sync request/response is the correct design for a stateless-utility and async is not needed. pricing.cpp makes no outbound network calls; it reads one local file and writes to stdout.

evaluations.title: Long-Running Process Handling
evaluations.reason: Archetype-N/A: no operations exceed 30 seconds. The request path is a single bounded file scan followed by one multiplication.

evaluations.title: Managed Databases
evaluations.reason: Surface gate: has_persistent_data_store=false. This system does not deploy a database - pricing.cpp reads a flat file via fopen; no DB driver, connection string, or DB resource exists (searched pricing.cpp, k8s/, Dockerfile).

evaluations.title: Backup and Recovery
evaluations.reason: Surface gate: no persistent state to back up. The only data file is the read-only /etc/pricing/rules.dat baked into the image; no volumes, PVCs, or AWS storage resources are declared. The source-of-truth problem for that file is captured under DATA-Q1.

evaluations.title: Encryption at Rest
evaluations.reason: Surface gate: has_at_rest_data_surface=false. No database, S3 bucket, EBS volume, or EFS file system; k8s/deployment.yaml declares no volumes or PVCs.

evaluations.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
evaluations.reason: Surface gate: has_persistent_data_store=false - no database engine is deployed, so there is no engine version to pin or EOL-check. Searched pricing.cpp, k8s/, Dockerfile, Makefile: no DB resource, no docker-compose database service, no migrations, no driver.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: Surface gate: has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false and no account-level IaC scope. CloudTrail is an account/organization-level service; this repo contains only Kubernetes manifests (searched repo root for *.tf, CDK, CloudFormation). CloudTrail evaluation belongs in the foundation infrastructure repo.

evaluations.title: Resource Tagging Governance
evaluations.reason: Surface gate: has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false - this repo provisions no AWS resources, so there are nothing to tag. Tagging governance belongs in the repo that owns the AWS infrastructure.

decomposition_strategy.context: The monolith here is a single 72-line CGI binary, so decomposition means replacing the CGI execution model rather than splitting a large codebase.

approaches.description: Keep one deployable unit; separate query parsing, rule lookup, and rendering into bounded modules with explicit interfaces, replacing strcpy/sprintf with bounds-checked C++ types.
approaches.rationale: Decomposition drivers are weak; the real gaps are memory safety, data sourcing, and delivery automation - all addressable inside one unit.

approaches.description: Stand up a modern pricing service alongside the CGI, shift a percentage of traffic, retire pricing.cgi once parity is proven.
approaches.rationale: Recommended as the follow-on once tests exist; the health endpoint (?sku=HEALTH&qty=1) gives a natural parity probe.

approaches.description: Keep the already-built container as-is, then selectively replace internals.
approaches.rationale: Partially already executed - Dockerfile and k8s/ manifests exist.

approaches.description: Replace the CGI wholesale in one cutover.
approaches.rationale: Generally recommended against; acceptable here only after characterization tests capture current pricing output, since README.md confirms there are no tests.

patterns.purpose: Isolate consumers from the CGI's HTML-only, unversioned response contract while a modern JSON API is introduced.
Not applicable - the service performs a read-only computation with no transaction.
Capture pricing-rule changes as an event history; rules are currently edited in-place on prod.
Separate the pricing core from the CGI/Apache adapter and the file-based rule adapter, making both swappable.

decomposition_strategy.calibrated_estimate: Strengthen-as-modular-monolith with memory-safety remediation is Low effort on code but gated by Medium effort on the missing test and pipeline foundations. Build the pipeline and characterization tests first.
